newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-England make most of lucky start vs NZ.
newsitem.headline: NZ SPORT-CRICKET-England make most of lucky start vs NZ.

text.p: England made the most of a lucky break when they set out in pursuit of 229 runs at the Basin Reserve on Tuesday to win the fifth one-day cricket international against New Zealand, and the one-day series.

Paceman Geoff Allott clean bowled England skipper Mike Atherton with the third ball of the innings, but in their celebration the Kiwis failed to notice that umpire Evan Watkin had called the delivery a no ball.
Television replays clearly showed Allott's foot was not fully over the crease line, as it needs to be to constitute a no ball.
Allott got some compensation when he took the prized scalp of Alec Stewart for 18 -- Stewart smashed a full toss straight to Dipak Patel at mid-on.
But Atherton made the most of his reprieve and took the New Zealand bowlers to task.
After 17 overs England were 75 for one, with Atherton on 31 and Nasser Hussain on 14.
New Zealand made a break-through immediately after the drinks break when Chris Harris enticed Hussain out of his crease and had him sharply stumped by Germon for 20.
After 19 overs, England were 81 for two with Graham Thorpe joining his captain in the middle.
Earlier, a terrific knock of 94 by Nathan Astle helped New Zealand to set a competitive total of 228 for eight from their 50 overs.
But New Zealand will have to bowl well on this good batting wicket to stop England from taking the match and the series.
